column1: # Transcribed bodies: name, recovered VA, the symbol the candidate defines, and the
# body's exact instruction count. verify_bodies.py resolves the symbol in
# ZolikaPatch.map and sweeps that many instructions linearly on both sides, so a
# row is a whole-body proof; a short decode on either side fails the row.
# Table rows are `table <recovered VA> <candidate symbol> <bytes>`: they name a
# table an arm registers with Bodies::RegisterTable, so an indexed absolute operand
# whose displacement is that table is compared as `table:<content hash>` on both
# sides instead of as a displacement. A displacement no row names keeps the literal
# ForceCarHeadlightShadows (source/vehicles.ixx): the shadow function's hook body and
# the per-model offset check it calls. The check (sub_1001AD20, 46 instructions, 139
# bytes) is transcribed; it walks the [HeadlightConeOffsets] hash table with
# `mov eax,[esi*4+0x1015ADBC]`, so ESI=511 reads the word immediately after the
# published shadow-function slot). The table registration is the extended 2,052-byte
# range so that read is compared too, and this tree reproduces the word as the same
# slot rather than a placeholder: it is defined immediately after the array, with the
# check's own resume word after it, in source/config.ixx. docs/rebuilt.md §2g.
# The four DFA file-API forwarders (source/launcher.ixx): `__cdecl` wrappers that
# push the caller's arguments and call the kernel32 entry through the original's
# IAT slot. The module has no IAT, so each `call ds:[…]` reads a slot the arm fills
# with the same function; the proof compares an absolute operand as a slot. The
# fifth, close_handle (0x10004790), keeps its C++ rebuild: its original stream is an
# EH4 frame (`__except_handler4`, scope table 0x10153FC0) with the funclet outside
# The native-script call layer (source/native.ixx). Its two SEH entries,
# sub_100038E0 (59 instructions) and sub_10003980 (52), are compiler output for a
# C function with __try/__except and are rebuilt rather than transcribed; their
# frames name image-specific handler addresses and cannot be compared this way.
# DrivebyFOVFix (source/misc.ixx): the shim and the FOV helper it calls. The helper
# calls the native layer's resolve entry instead of the original's sub_10003980;
# the proof compares a call as an immediate, so the body is whole.
# BadPlayerModelCrashFix (source/stability.ixx): the site's trampoline, the payload
# it calls and the two native wrappers of its GTAC.dll diagnostic. The wrappers'
# sub_100038E0) are transcribed in source/native.ixx and source/shared.ixx and
# proved by their own rows above; the payload's fallback calls the layer's copy of
# sub_1005B3F0 through a forwarder, so there is no second row for it.
# The model-name lookup (0x10003F00): 21 instructions, two indexed absolute table
# operands (`push [table + esi*4]`, `mov eax, [table + esi*4]`). The arm registers
# the 38,455-entry table with Bodies::RegisterTable (0x100DE770, 153820 bytes), so
# the comparator resolves both operands through the registry and compares the
# table's contents instead of its displacement. The table row below is the offline
# projection of that registration: recovered VA, the candidate symbol the linker map
# resolves, and the registered length. docs/rebuilt.md §2b.
# Patch4RemoveModChecks (source/misc.ixx): the shared GFWL/Patch4 stub. Its
# helper (sub_10005340, 145 instructions) is compiler output and is rebuilt; the
# same recovered VA is already proven for loading.ixx's RemoveGFWLUpdatePopup arm.
# CopSirensFlag (source/misc.ixx): the two model-check shims, the shared IDE
# parser hook and both model checks. The checks read the +siren table as a plain
# absolute the registry canonicalises with the base register still compared. The
# table row is the offline projection of the arm's RegisterTable call.
# The IDE parser payload (sub_10003FA0, 92 instructions, 314 bytes) is transcribed.
# It fills four 512-slot tables and touches three registered ones: the +siren list
# above, the wheelangle model/angle pair below, and the +popuplights list here. It
# reads each list through `[eax+table]` (a base plus displacement, the §2d shape) and
# writes it through `[ecx*4+table]` (an indexed absolute, the §2b shape); the slot-0
# entry check is a plain absolute and compares as an `abs` slot. The table row is the
# offline projection of the arm's RegisterTable call; the table is all-zero at load in
# PopupHeadlightsFlag (source/misc.ixx): the EAX site's shim, its EDX twin and the
# checker itself. The twin's pattern is absent on 1.0.8.0 (the original's own second
# site is a build-specific row) but the body is still proven.
# The checker (sub_10044310, 125 instructions, 534 bytes) is transcribed. It reads
# the [PopupLightAngles] tables as eight interleaved 64-row columns, so seven of each
# eight displacements are four bytes into the array rather than at its base: the
# registry resolves a displacement *inside* a registered table to that table plus the
# offset, and the offset is still compared (a changed column is an instruction
# difference). The two table rows are the offline projection of the arm's
# RegisterTable calls -- Config's own arrays, which the loader preamble's reader
# fills, not copies. The +popuplights list it walks is the table row above.
# NewMemorySystem (source/loading.ixx): the ten methods of the allocator vtable
# (original 0x100B5038) that are written as instruction streams. Its three arena
# methods (0x10038360 allocate, 0x10038430 free, 0x100385A0 membership) carry the
# compiler's frames, cmov sequences and hash-map code and are rebuilt in C++, so
# they have no rows (docs/parity.md). nms_sync is the table's 0x100057F0 slot: the
# same two instructions as audio.ixx's better_mp_sync row, duplicated because a
# table in this unit cannot name a body internal to another unit.
# Its two update bodies (0x10051890, 0x100518D0) are compiled in the original and
# are rebuilt in C++, so they have no rows (docs/parity.md).
# instructions to its tail jump. The prepare step (0x10051FD0), the converter
# (0x10051B30) and the two read hooks it installs (0x10051A90, 0x10051AD0) are
# compiled C in the original -- file IO, a std::string path build with the TLS
# static-init guards and /GS frames -- and are rebuilt in C++, so they have no rows
# RestoreDeathMusic (source/audio.ixx): the gate body and the three native-script
# wrappers it answers through, transcribed because the layer's own four pieces
# forwarders. The install body (sub_10050AD0, 75 instructions to its `ret`) is
# rebuilt: it is compiler output with an EH4 frame whose clock/seed block calls the
# CRT's image-internal helpers, so it has no row (docs/parity.md).
# MouseFix (source/audio.ixx): all eight pieces are transcribed. The two site
# bodies call their helpers directly (the call target is an immediate on both
# sides, which is what the proof compares), and the advance helper's only indirect
# call is the game's VirtualProtect through the published slot -- the original's
# `FF 15` to its own IAT slot, compared as a memory operand.
# LoadDLCs (source/loading.ixx): the loader callback's replacement and the DLC
# manager's initialisation tail. The discovery pass the tail calls (0x10023150) is
# a rebuild - compiled code with a /GS frame, TLS static-init guards and CRT calls -
# The steer/engine/plane consumer (0x10004C70, 320 instructions) and the two tables
# it walks. Every operand is an absolute slot except the two indexed absolutes into
# the wheelangle model/angle tables, which are registered: `table` rows below pair
# the recovered VA with the candidate symbol the linker map resolves (a C name,
# because the arrays are `extern "C"` in misc.ixx where the IDE parser hook fills
# them) and the length there (512 dwords). Both tables are all-zero at load in the
# original and here, so the content check pins "reads a zero-filled table registered
# for this row"; which table each operand reads is pinned by the manifest pairing and
# Its model-registry lookup (sub_10003F40) is transcribed too.
# GarageModelFix (source/vehicles.ixx): both site bodies and the two helpers they
# call, all transcribed. The colour copy reads the model-info array and the
# CitizenIV flag; the lookup makes the two dword_10159C0C calls and carries the
# /GS frame the original's compiled C has.
# counter, the 0x10-byte name copy, and the five site bodies (A-C at the livery
# anchor, D/E at the collector). The hasher and the counter call the original's
# own resolver through a forwarder and the bounded formatter through the rebuilt
# sub_10001280; the proof compares a call as an immediate.
# CutsceneFixes (source/graphics.ixx): chain B's body, the original's sub_100388C0.
# 146 is the count to its `ret 4` at 0x10038B0D, which is 592 bytes; the restore
# block at 0x10038B10..0x10038B3F follows that `ret` and is reached only by the six
# `ja` exits, so the linear sweep does not decode it. The body's `call` names the
# local resolve forwarder that stands in for sub_10003980, which is rebuilt as C in
# source/native.ixx; the proof compares a call as an immediate.
# OutOfCommissionFix (source/ooc.ixx): the branch body the E9 at game 0xA22E97
# jumps to (7 instructions) and the mounting wrapper the E8 at 0xB70733 is
# retargeted to (41 to its `ret`, 0x1004C350..0x1004C3BF). The key's remaining
# rebuilt pieces are compiler output -- the init (sub_1004B750, EH + C++
# containers) and the key's own handler (sub_1004C3F0, 4199 instructions with an
# EH4 frame) -- and have no rows (docs/parity.md); the decoder pair is transcribed
# below and the archive builder with its twelve helpers in the block at the end of
# The decoder pair (source/ooc.ixx): an interpreter with sixteen exits and no
# register contract beyond "ECX in, EAX out", no exception frame, no TLS static-init
# guard and no indexed absolute operand, so it is transcribed whole. The opcode
# step's four CRT `memcpy` calls go through a forwarder (the inline assembler
# refuses `call memcpy`); the driver's Adler-32 loop is inline in the original, not
# a call, so its 5552-byte block structure is transcribed too. docs/rebuilt.md.
# HighQualityReflections (source/graphics.ixx): the detour body the E9 at game
# 0xC51311 jumps to. 157 instructions to its `jmp [resume]` (858 bytes): eight
# register saves, the twelve builder calls with the eight restores after each of
# the first eleven, and the tail jump. The site's own call is at match+0x0E, so
# the resume it publishes is match+0x13 (the `push 0` after that call).
# The bounded formatter (source/stability.ixx): the original's single formatter,
# transcribed whole. sub_10001280 is the wrapper (the other modules reach it through
# a six-byte forwarder on zpatch_format_entry), sub_10001240 the printf-engine call
# -- its `call ds:[__stdio_common_vsprintf]` is a slot here, because the static CRT
# has no IAT for the engine -- and sub_10001230 the two-dword options block it reads.
# The three C++ `_vsnprintf_s` rebuilds this replaces are gone; docs/rebuilt.md.
# NewSavesCompatibility's two installed hooks (source/loading.ixx): the read at game
# 0x7D8C50 and the second LoadData at 0x8DA090. Both were C++ rebuilds; the /GS
# frames, the EAX the hooks answer with and the unconditional second call are now
# LoadDLCs' discovery pass (source/loading.ixx): 223 instructions to its `ret`, with
# no EH frame, no TLS static-init guard and no indexed absolute operand -- the one
# rebuilt piece that was transcribable, so it is transcribed. Its IAT operands are
# the five slots the arm fills; its two `call` targets are the allocation/memset
# forwarders and the shared formatter. docs/rebuilt.md.
# The OOC archive builder (source/ooc.ixx) and its twelve internal helpers: what was
# the last class-D piece. Its stream has no exception frame and no TLS static-init
# guard, and every one of the twelve helpers is itself a plain stream -- SSE stores,
# cmov, direct `E8`s, EBP/ECX-relative -- so the whole graph is transcribed here and
# the class-D objection ("every call lands in another rebuild") no longer holds. The
# CRT boundaries (operator new, memset, memcpy, free) are cdecl forwarders, and the
# vector's element-destroy loop (0x1005CD50) stays rebuilt; docs/rebuilt.md 2h.
# FreezeCarFix / DebugPrintSpawns (source/vehicles.ixx): the spawn guard, the ten
# factory-dispatch thunks and the 394-instruction spawn probe the original's handler
# 0x10037C70 installs through sixteen `E8` detours (seventeen rows: the primary and
# its short prefix name the same site). The probe's name/who/print helpers are
# compiler output and rebuilt in C++; its formatter is the body source/stability.ixx
# VRAMFix (source/misc.ixx): the argument/verdict shim the original's handler
# 0x1004AAE0 jumps to from its single matched site. Its verdict helper is compiler
# output and rebuilt in C++. docs/parity.md.
# AddOptionsInMenu / IVMenuAPI (source/menu.ixx): the writer 0x1001EDE0 and the
# death-music installer 0x10050BD0 are the two handlers the original's config
# walker calls once the companion library is loaded; both are transcribed. The
# death-music gate and its three native-script wrappers are the same recovered
# pieces source/audio.ixx carries for RestoreDeathMusic (its copies have internal
# linkage, so this module carries its own; only one copy is live per
# configuration). The four callbacks are the function pointers the two
# AddIVMenuOption registrations pass. sub_1001ECB0 and sub_10050AD0 are compiler
# output (EH4 frame + TLS static-init guard) and rebuilt in C++; no rows.
# The ZMenuIV version guard 0x10052300 is not part of this key: the walker calls
# it unconditionally at 0x1005527B. It is a plain /GS body, so it is transcribed
